ruling.explanation:
Rider R-71451 and Driver D-78879: the rider's route-deviation claim succeeds in part. The platform's recorded distances put the trip at 8.3 km against a recommended 6.7 km, a deviation of 1.60 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix are unavailable. The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only LTA advisory covering the recommended road (Marymount Road, Bishan Road to Thomson Road) does overlap the trip window, but its type is NONE and its own message records no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-5 throughout; NONE is not a kind POL-RD-23 recognises, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's bare assertion of traffic with no supporting data does not justify a reroute, so the driver's 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' cannot carry the justification rows (a) or (b) would need. Notice of the deviation was also not given as POL-RD-21 requires: the trip record's messages_during_trip list is empty, in_app_calls is empty, and the chat log's only two entries are pre-pickup logistics sent at 08:06 and 08:07, before the 08:09 trip start and well before the 08:16 deviation; the driver's own 'Didn't think need to say' confirms it. With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over 1 km, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and pays the excess distance fare in full: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.152, rounded to the cent, 1.15 SGD, without surge. The rider's 'about $3' is not the policy measure, and the 1.2x surge (2.51 SGD) and the 21-minute time fare (3.78 SGD) are not part of a route-deviation remedy, so the recovery is 1.15 SGD, not the whole contested 3.00 SGD. The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has yet been returned. On who decides: the contested value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so the 0.95 band is not engaged; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), so no escalation is required and the record is complete on every artifact at full weight. The rider therefore is owed 1.15 SGD of the contested amount, and this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.15 SGD with no driver compensation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of your accounts, and the platform's own record, agree on what matters here. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the platform's recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km 5.2 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 4.6 km = 0.60 km, and it sets the tolerance at 1.0 km. A 0.60 km deviation is within tolerance, and neither party asks the judge to depart from those figures. POL-RD-24 row (e) therefore governs: the reroute was not traffic-justified — the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05002-01) is type NONE, and although it covers Bedok Road (the recommended road) and the trip window, it records no closure, congestion or incident, so POL-RD-23 is not satisfied and the driver's assertion of slow traffic does not stand in for that data — and a non-justified deviation of 1 km or less returns no refund. The traffic-justified branch reaches the same result: row (c) also returns no refund on a deviation of 1 km or less, so no refund is payable whether or not the reroute was justified. On the driver's duty to notify under POL-RD-21, the chat log (EV-CHAT-05002) holds two messages, both sent at 11:26 and both about the pickup point, the deviation was detected at 11:30:14, in_app_calls is empty, and no call recording establishes a verbal notice — so an agreed deviation is not made out; but within tolerance no refund turns on notice. The rider's figure of $2.00 is not one POL-RD-24 measures: the excess distance fare would be 0.60 × per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.43 SGD, and it does not arise at all because the deviation is within tolerance. The rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the metered fare of 9.42 SGD was charged and no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The driver's profile plays no part: POL-GEN-01 makes its fields context only and driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0. The contested value is 2.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this ruling is final at any confidence, and every artifact POL-RD-24 reads is present and COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26's escalation does not arise.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the rider is owed the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD, and nothing more. Why.

1) The deviation is established. POL-RD-22 measures it as the platform's recorded actual distance minus the recorded recommended distance: 9.5 km − 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004). POL-RD-22's tolerance is 1.0 km, so 1.40 km is over tolerance and the within-tolerance no-refund rows are shut out. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) is used only to show which route was taken: its fixes run along Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West between 08:42:52 and 08:53:22, immediately after the platform logged the departure from the recommended route at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit (08:42:55) and immediately before the logged rejoin at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West (08:53:16). The reroute is real.

2) The driver did not inform the rider. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation (08:42:55). EV-CHAT-05004 carries only two messages, both before the trip started and both about the pickup point; EV-TRIP-05004 records messages_during_trip as empty and in_app_calls as empty. No recorded call can carry a verbal notice. The driver's own statement concedes it: 'Forgot to inform, sorry.' Row (a) of the refund matrix, the only no-refund row for an over-tolerance deviation, is therefore unavailable.

3) The traffic question does not change the money. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05004-01 reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the PIE towards Changi between the Clementi Avenue 6 exit and the Clementi Road exit, with a window (08:15:42–09:27:22) that overlaps the trip (08:37:22–08:55:22). Road, direction of travel and location all sit on the recommended route segment, so POL-RD-23's requirement that the advisory intersect the recommended route and overlap the window is satisfied on this record and the reroute is traffic-justified — row (b). Even if it were not, the case would fall in row (d). Both rows pay the same thing: the excess distance fare (POL-RD-24).

4) The quantum. POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare as deviation distance × fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure EV-FARE-05004's own money block carries. The rider's asserted 4.00 SGD is his own estimate and is not the measure POL-RD-24 provides; the balance of that claim is refused. Nothing has been returned yet (EV-FARE-05004: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so the amount is still outstanding.

5) Outcome. The rider filed, and he is owed less than the 4.00 SGD he contested, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of the part owed: 1.01 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null. A route deviation has no referral clause in this version, so referrals is empty. Confidence 0.90: every artifact that carries the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05004, EV-FARE-05004, EV-CHAT-05004) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, the deviation and its measure are agreed on both sides, and the only incidental open point — whether the advisory precisely overlays the recommended segment — does not affect the amount either way.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and to the driver. WHAT IS AGREED. The recommended route was 10.00 km and the trip as driven was 11.40 km (EV-TRIP-05003). The deviation is therefore 1.40 km (POL-RD-22), above the 1.00 km tolerance, and neither side disputes it; the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05003) shows the same movement, the vehicle leaving the CTE at Bendemeer Road at 19:00:36 and rejoining at Upper Serangoon Road/Braddell Road at 19:11:06. WAS THE REROUTE TRAFFIC-JUSTIFIED? Yes (POL-RD-23). The LTA traffic advisory in the record (EV-ADVIS-05003-01, weight 1.0, complete) reports an accident on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which covers this trip's 18:49:44-19:12:44 window. The recommended route in the trip record runs along the CTE towards SLE (optimal_route_via), and the platform's own deviation event records that the recommended route at the point the driver left it was the CTE. The accident therefore lies on that CTE stretch, in the direction of travel, inside the trip window, and the advisory intersects the recommended route. The rider is right that the platform's derived reading left this 'undetermined' and the record does not decide it for the parties, but POL-RD-23 asks the decision to be made from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip, and on those it does intersect. I do not find this a fact the record cannot establish, and I decline to escalate on the rider's POL-GEN-26 ground, and equally on the driver's alternative request to escalate on the same point. WAS THE RIDER INFORMED AND DID THE RIDER AGREE? Yes (POL-RD-21). The driver's in-app message MSG-05003-003 ('CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster.', EV-CHAT-05003) was sent 18:57:46 and read 18:58:03, about three minutes before the 19:00:36 deviation. The rider replied MSG-05003-004 ('Ok sure, thanks for telling') at 18:58:26, read 18:58:49. The rider argues this is a bare acknowledgment, not agreement to 1.40 km of extra metered distance. POL-RD-21 answers it: where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed. The log confirms it, so the deviation was agreed, and the case does not fall outside POL-RD-24's rows on that ground. WHICH ROW (POL-RD-24). Exactly one row applies. Traffic-justified; rider informed and agreed; deviation over 1.00 km: row (a), no refund. The rider's claim for 4.50 SGD is not supported. For completeness, the refund rows would have capped recovery at the excess distance fare: 1.40 km x the 0.72 SGD per km rate = 1.01 SGD, without surge, far below the 4.50 SGD claimed and against a 22.60 SGD fare; the rider's own advocate conceded that figure. The driver's point that no row could award 4.50 SGD is correct but does not arise. The rider's further point that the reroute was not actually faster (23.0 minutes against the recommended 20.2 minutes) is accurate but immaterial: POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute on the traffic data, not on whether it saved time. DECISION (POL-GEN-03). The rider filed, so the ruling is read against the rider's claim. That claim is not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, no refund, no driver compensation, and no money moves - the 22.60 SGD fare already charged stands. WHO DECIDES (POL-RD-25, POL-GEN-22). The contested value is 4.50 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band; the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 0, so the 0.95 uplift does not bite; the route-deviation bar is 0.80 and this ruling is issued at 0.85. The AI's 2 km deviation limit is not applied (thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), and 1.40 km would clear it in any event. No safety flag applies, and a route deviation carries no referral clause, so there is no referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the rider filed this dispute contesting 5.00 SGD of a metered fare of 23.04 SGD, and the rider is owed part of what was charged — 1.56 SGD — not the whole 5.00 SGD.

How the deviation is measured (both sides agree, and I accept it): POL-RD-22 fixes the distance as the platform's recorded figures, 13.8 km actual minus 12.1 km recommended = 1.70 km. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply. The 1.70 km is not disputed, and the GPS trace is used only to show which roads were taken (Upper Serangoon Road from 10:21:38, rejoin at 10:35:21), not to re-measure distance, exactly as POL-RD-22 directs.

Why the driver's 'no refund' case fails (POL-RD-21): POL-RD-21 permits a traffic reroute only if the driver informs the rider by in-app chat 'before or at the point of deviation.' The platform logged the deviation at 10:21:30; the driver's explaining message (MSG-05005-003, 'KPE got breakdown ... so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead') was sent at 10:24:30 — about three minutes after the turn. Notice after the turn is not notice before or at the deviation, so the rider was not informed within the meaning of POL-RD-21, and the rider's 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 answers a message that came too late. An acknowledgment of a turn already taken is not the (a)-row agreement to a deviation the rider could still refuse. The driver's statement that he informed the passenger 'before I changed route' is contradicted by the chat log's own timestamps.

Why the outcome is still a refund whichever way traffic justification goes (POL-RD-23, POL-RD-24): the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05005-01) is a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the KPE — an admissible 'incident' type under POL-RD-23 — with a validity window (09:59:38 to 10:54:38) that overlaps the trip. Whether or not it is treated as lying on the recommended route (its own record leaves that 'undetermined'), the outcome is the same: if traffic-justified, row (b) applies (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km); if not, row (d) applies (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km). Both rows return the excess distance fare, so the open route-intersection point is not outcome-determinative and no POL-GEN-26 escalation is needed to resolve it.

The sum awarded (POL-RD-24): the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564, rounded to 1.56 SGD. That is the only component of the 23.04 SGD fare attributable to the extra distance (base 3.80 + distance 12.70 + time 5.64 + platform fee 0.90, no surge, no ERP, no waiting fee). No row of the matrix returns the whole fare, and nothing touches the base, time or platform lines, so the rider's round 5.00 SGD figure over-states the entitlement by 3.44 SGD. Since the rider filed and is owed part of the contested charge, the result is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.56 SGD, and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

Confidence and forum (POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25): the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no elevated threshold applies; POL-RD-25 sets the route-deviation bar at 0.80, POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off and the 1.70 km deviation is under 2 km in any event, and every artifact I relied on — trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, traffic advisory — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. My confidence is 0.85. No clause in this version produces a referral on a route deviation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

This is a route-deviation dispute about 1.37 SGD, and it is decided on the platform's own records, all of which the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at full weight.

What is not in dispute. The recommended route was 12.7 km (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street) and the driver actually covered 14.6 km (via West Coast Highway, Pasir Panjang Road, Telok Blangah Road). Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the recorded actual distance minus the recorded recommended distance: 14.6 - 12.7 = 1.90 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace's own 12.318 km is not used to re-measure the distance, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length. So this is a deviation case, not a within-tolerance one.

The driver did inform the rider, and the rider agreed. MSG-05006-003 was sent in-app at 18:01:46 ('Miss, AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?'), the platform's route_deviation_detected event is timed at 18:05:06, and the rider answered 'ok' at 18:02:11. The notice preceded the deviation and gave a brief reason, and the chat log records the rider's acknowledgment, which under POL-RD-21 makes the deviation agreed. The rider's later remark that the AYE looked clear does not unmake the 'ok' she gave in the log before the turn.

But agreement and notice are not enough. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 - no refund - also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and POL-RD-23 allows that only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA record for the recommended segment (AYE towards City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct) covers the trip window but is advisory type NONE, with speed bands 4-6 and a message that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded; 28-42 km/h on the corridor is not congestion by the policy's own vocabulary. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's report of a jam does not carry row (a). The only closure-kind advisory in the record is the lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah - a road on the route the driver chose, not on the recommended route - so it does not satisfy POL-RD-23 either. The drivers' alternative escalation argument fails on the same point: the advisory's intersection with the recommended route is answerable from its road, direction and location against the trip, and the answer is no, so there is no open question under POL-GEN-26 to send to a reviewer.

That leaves row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, refund of the excess distance fare in full. The figure is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD, which is exactly the sum the fare ledger records as the excess distance fare and as the amount refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 19 Aug 2026 at 01:56:34 (fare_adjusted).

Because the driver filed this dispute to claw back a refund the rider is owed, the driver's claim fails. Under POL-GEN-03 and the filing frame, the outcome is NO_ACTION - party-relative, the present state stands - and both amounts are null. The 1.37 SGD stays with the rider. The contested value is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so this ruling is final at any confidence, and the agreement requirement, the rider's overall reliability and the driver's history on either profile are context only under POL-GEN-01 and do not decide this trip. No referral clause applies to a route deviation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider: you complained that on the 20 Aug 2026 trip from Northpoint City to The Seletar Mall the driver took Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu instead of the recommended Seletar Road, and you asked for SGD 2.50 back. You are right that the detour happened: the trip record logs a route_deviation_detected at 13:28:02 and a rejoin at 13:35:58, and the driver-device GPS trace runs through Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu precisely where the recommended route ran via Seletar Road. You are right too that the driver did not tell you about it - the platform chat log carries 0 messages and no call recording exists in the record, so POL-RD-21's notice obligation is not made out - and right that the LTA advisory for the Seletar Road corridor shows type NONE, so 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' is the bare assertion POL-RD-23 says does not justify a reroute.

But the refund turns on the size of the deviation, and POL-RD-22 measures that from the platform's own recorded distances: 8.3 km actual minus 7.3 km recommended = 1.00 km. The same clause puts 'a deviation of 1.0 km or less' within tolerance, and 1.00 km sits exactly on that line, so it is within tolerance, not over it. POL-RD-24 says exactly one row applies, and at a deviation of 1 km or less the only open rows are (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed) and (e) (not traffic-justified) - both say no refund, within tolerance. Because the LTA record shows no congestion, incident or closure, your case falls in row (e). The excess-distance figure you and the driver both correctly identify - 1.00 km x SGD 0.72 per km = SGD 0.72, without surge - is therefore not refundable, and neither is any part of the SGD 12.65 metered fare that was charged to you (refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

The boundary point you raise is answered by the policy itself. POL-RD-22 draws a bright line at '1.0 km or less', and the recorded distances (8.3 km and 7.3 km) compute to a deviation of 1.00 km - on the tolerant side of that line, and given in the case's own derived facts as within_tolerance. That is a measurement the policy requires to be taken from these recorded distances, not a gap the record leaves open; and your alternative escalation fails for the same reason, because rows (c) and (e) both close the case and no fact POL-RD-24 needs is missing or impaired (the trip record, fare breakdown, chat log, GPS trace and traffic advisory are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged).

To the driver: the detour is confirmed on the record, you did not notify the rider, and 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' is not a POL-RD-23 traffic justification. Your claim nonetheless succeeds only because the deviation of 1.00 km is within the 1.0 km tolerance the policy allows, so the SGD 12.65 charge stands as it is.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands - NO_ACTION, with no amount refunded to the rider and no compensation payable to the driver. (Confidence 0.90; the deciding facts - the recorded deviation distance and the absence of any justifying traffic condition - rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, and the case is below the SGD 10.00 finality threshold with a 0.80 route-deviation bar under POL-RD-25.)

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Each side is partly right, but the rule that decides this case sends it to a human reviewer rather than to either party's pocket.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The driver left the recommended route at the KPE / Sims Way exit at 19:37:02 and rejoined at Upper Serangoon Road / Hougang Avenue 1 at 19:50:37. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is measured on the platform's recorded distances, 11.4 km actual against 9.9 km recommended = 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD (POL-RD-24, excess_distance_fare formula, no surge) - exactly the sum refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings at 20:48:23 (refund_issued_sgd 1.08; total trip charge 22.11 SGD).

NOTICE AND AGREEMENT (POL-RD-21). The driver's chat at 19:34:22, 'Miss, KPE very jam after Sims Way, I come out at Sims Ave and go Aljunied ok? Faster', preceded the exit on any timestamp, so the notice limb is met - the driver is right on that, and the finding stands. But the rider answered at 19:34:52, 'No need, pls just stay on KPE, I don't mind the jam', and repeated the objection at 19:38:22. POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. There is no acknowledgment here. The deviation is therefore informed but not agreed.

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION (POL-RD-23). The LTA record (EV-ADVIS-05008-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (towards TPE) after the Sims Way exit, valid 19:09:23 to 20:19:23 and so overlapping the trip window (19:29:23 to 19:52:23). That road is the recommended route's own road, the direction is the route's direction of travel, and the location is the recommended route immediately beyond the point the trip record itself marks as the deviation - the same jam the driver cited at the time. The package left this intersection to the judge because the derived intersects_route and justifies_reroute fields are null; deciding it on road, direction and location as POL-RD-23 directs, I find the advisory intersects the recommended route and the reroute was traffic-justified.

THE MATRIX (POL-RD-24) - NO ROW APPLIES. Row (a) needs the rider to have agreed; she did not. Row (b) needs the rider not to have been informed; she was. Rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less; it is 1.50 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified; it was. POL-RD-24 says that a case fitting no row - its own example being 'informed but the rider objected' - is escalated under POL-GEN-26. That is this case.

OUTCOME. ESCALATE is terminal (POL-GEN-03): no money issues to either side, and the 1.08 SGD is held by the platform - not paid back to the driver and not released to the rider - pending a human reviewer.

THE DRIVER'S CLAIMS. The findings on notice, on traffic justification and on the 1.50 km deviation are accepted, as is the point that the excess distance fare measures 1.08 SGD. They do not produce the payment the driver asks for. The 1.08 SGD cannot come back to the driver: no row of POL-RD-24 licenses DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION would only preserve the present state, never restore a charge - and in any event this case fits no no-refund row. The driver's alternative claim is accepted: the most the rider's objection can do is send the money to a human reviewer, and that is what happens here.

THE RIDER'S CLAIMS. Her arithmetic and ledger facts (1.50 km x 0.72 = 1.08 SGD; refund_issued_sgd 1.08; PARTIALLY_REFUNDED) are accepted, and she is right that row (a) is unavailable for want of her agreement. But the rows that would pay that 1.08 SGD to her each fail on their own condition - row (b) because she was informed, row (d) because the reroute was traffic-justified - so the money does not simply stay with her either; POL-RD-24 escalates it. Her reading of the LTA package as leaving the route intersection to the judge is correct and is answered above; that finding removes row (d) but converts nothing into a payment to the driver, which is her central point and it is upheld.

EVIDENCE WEIGHT. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and LTA advisory all carry weight 1.0 and are complete, so nothing under POL-GEN-02 lowers confidence; the confidence stated is above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. No clause in this category produces a referral on a route deviation, so the referrals list is empty.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER (not referrals): whether a driver who proceeds after an express refusal should still keep the excess distance fare, and whether the interim 1.08 SGD adjustment should be finalised or reversed.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the record decides this case, and I find for the rider in part.

Route and deviation. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05010, weight 1.0, no issues) shows the recommended route ran via the East Coast Parkway at 19.7 km, while the route actually driven went via the PIE, Sims Way and Lavender Street over 22.0 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation as the platform's recorded actual distance minus its recorded optimal distance: 22.0 - 19.7 = 2.30 km, well over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The sparse GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance; it is used only to show which route was taken and when, which is what POL-RD-22 permits, and it confirms a single bounded departure at 14:36:54 and a rejoin at 14:58:48, not a detour for the whole ride.

Traffic justification. POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended segment at the trip time. The only traffic data, EV-ADVIS-05010-01, covers exactly that ECP segment and overlaps the trip window, and records type NONE with speed bands 5-7 - no incident, roadwork or closure. The driver's statement that "ECP sometimes jam near Marina" is a bare assertion of traffic, and POL-RD-23 says in terms that such an assertion, with no supporting data, does not justify a reroute. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified.

Notice. POL-RD-21 also required the driver to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat (or a recorded verbal notice) before or at the point of deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05010) ends at 14:32:20, before the trip even started; trip_record.derived.v7.messages_during_trip is empty and in_app_calls is empty. There is no notice and no acknowledgment, and the rider's silence in the car is not agreement. The driver's "passenger never say anything" does not answer a duty that POL-RD-21 places on the driver.

Remedy. Those findings place the case in row (d) of POL-RD-24 - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That is 2.30 km x 0.92 SGD/km (the per-km rate in the fare breakdown, EV-FARE-05010) = 2.116, rounded to 2.12 SGD, with no surge (surge_amount 0.00, surge_multiplier 1.0). No row of POL-RD-24 returns a whole metered fare, so the rider's demand for the entire 36.30 SGD cannot be granted: the remaining 34.18 SGD of the fare stands. Nothing has already been returned (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED), so 2.12 SGD is payable to the rider.

Decision and confidence.
